clue.text: Sneakily managing to get rid of women's sport

indicators.note: getting rid of something means it is removed from the word before it

parts.note: to wangle something is to manage it by trickery
W is the standard abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Someone cunningly arranges for a women's sporting event to be scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing with rod and line is a popular pastime counted among field sports.

clue.text: Country on the up? Why pulling out shows arrogance

indicators.note: pulling out means the letter is withdrawn
in a down clue on the up means the word reads upwards

parts.note: Syria is a country
Y sounds like why

explanation.surface: A country is prospering, so why is it pulling out of talks and behaving arrogantly?
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the up' gives AIRYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs is acting superior, so airs are a show of haughtiness.

clue.text: Government exposed, having to resolve this person's issue over introduction of algorithm

definitions.text: Government exposed, having to resolve this person's issue over introduction of algorithm

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: will is resolve or determination

indicators.note: over here means the I'M goes over and around the next letter

parts.note: this person is, said by the person, is I'm

indicators.note: introduction of picks the first letter

parts.note: a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: The government is embarrassed into fixing the exam grades fiasco caused by an algorithm.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate definition: the whole clue describes the education secretary in 2020, when an algorithm downgraded A-level results. 'over' is read as I'M enclosing the A.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the education secretary blamed for the 2020 exam-grading algorithm fiasco.

clue.text: Damage caused by mutation originally, mate — one's on top of it

indicators.note: in a down clue being on top of means coming first

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter

parts.note: to mate is to pair

explanation.surface: Harm caused by a genetic mutation, and a friend says it's under control.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or spoil, doing harm to something.

clue.text: Something wrong? Idiot left to shaft children

indicators.note: to shaft here means to drive into, so left pierces the idiot

parts.note: git is British slang for an idiot

explanation.surface: Is something amiss? A fool has left to cheat the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shaft' puts L into GIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a minor fault or malfunction, a small problem.

clue.text: Wrongly attempt to back current Conservative leader — it makes no sense

parts.note: ill can mean badly or wrongly, as in ill-advised

indicators.note: to back here means the word for an attempt is written backwards

parts.note: a go is an attempt
I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Supporting the current Tory leader would be a mistake, the speaker says, since it is senseless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' turns GO into OG.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogic is faulty reasoning, a thing that does not hold together as an argument.

clue.text: Had a feeling it worked with United

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded into a different form

explanation.surface: A fan sensed a plan would work with Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges IT + UNITED.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to sense or know by instinct, without reasoning.

clue.text: Extremely wary crossing lake in case

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the word for in case goes either side

parts.note: lest means in case, for fear that
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Someone is very cautious about crossing a lake, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' belongs to the definition (most wary), not an instruction to take end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Leery means suspicious or wary, and this is its superlative, most cautious.

clue.text: Ugh! A putdown with a hint of absurdity, say? Embarrassed, we don't want to hear any more

definitions.text: we don't want to hear any more

indicators.note: embarrassed letters are disturbed and put in a different order
a hint of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An embarrassed audience groans at a putdown that hints at the absurd: enough already!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embarrassed' rearranges UGH, A, PUTDOWN, A (first of absurdity) and SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: This blunt phrase is a rude demand that a speaker leave and stop talking.

clue.text: Made mistake in discussion before everything's gone belly up — pantomime!

indicators.note: in discussion means as heard in speech

parts.note: to sin is to do wrong, so made a mistake gives sinned
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: belly up means turned over, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: all is everything

explanation.surface: After a slip in conversation, everything collapses: what a farce!
explanation.walkthrough: SINNED sounds like CIND-. 'gone belly up' turns ALL into LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: This rags-to-riches fairy tale is the most popular British pantomime, a family stage show at Christmas.

clue.text: Put one's foot down? Minister's revolting

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a minister of religion; the 's stands for 'is'
people up in arms or risen in revolt are said to be up

explanation.surface: A government minister is in open rebellion, and someone takes a firm stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot down' is read literally as pressing the accelerator.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the accelerator pedal hard makes an engine race, which is what drivers call making it roar.

clue.text: Generally at sea

definitions.meaning: the main is an old word for the open ocean, so this means out on the ocean

explanation.surface: Generally at sea
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means mostly, and literally means out on the ocean, since the main is poetic for the open water.

clue.text: One minister, I finally concluded, can work without discernment

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: to work clay or dough is to shape it, so these letters are reshaped
finally picks the last letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A minister who has finally reached a decision says he can do the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like part of the surface ('can work') but is fodder; 'work' alone rearranges MINISTER, I, D and CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without discernment means failing to distinguish or choose carefully, which is being random or undiscriminating.

clue.text: Admire loos, possibly this one

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to appreciate some lavatories, perhaps this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ADMIRE LOOS, and the result is itself one of the loos.
explanation.definitionFit: A women's public toilet is one of the loos you might admire, so the clue describes itself.

clue.text: Greedy artist has chop for starter

indicators.note: chopping the starter means removing the first letter

parts.note: David is a painter, Jacques-Louis David, or David Hockney

explanation.surface: A greedy painter tucks into a chop as his first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chop for starter' reads like a menu but removes the first letter of DAVID.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid person is eager and keen for more, like a greedy one.

clue.text: In trouble, use padre's influence

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: When you're in difficulty, call on the chaplain's sway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In trouble' rearranges USE PADRE; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To influence someone is to bring them round to your view, to win them over.

clue.text: Tributary of Lune fit for swimming around noon

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the other one
swimming letters move about freely

explanation.surface: A branch of the river Lune is suitable for a dip around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lune is a river in north-west England. 'for swimming' rearranges LUNE FIT, which goes 'around' N.
explanation.definitionFit: An influent is a stream flowing into a larger one, a feeder river.

clue.text: Lira included in coinage for the Americas

indicators.note: included in means put inside the word that follows

parts.note: a coinage is a newly invented word, a new word
L is the abbreviation for lira, the old Italian currency

explanation.surface: Italian money is used in coins made for the American market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coinage' looks like money but means an invented term.
explanation.definitionFit: Europeans named the Americas this, contrasting them with the Old World of Europe, Asia and Africa.

clue.text: Brit in India, one smoothing over quarrel at last?

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: over here means the sander goes over and around the letter

parts.note: a sander is a tool that smooths surfaces

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A Briton in India smooths over a quarrel at last.
explanation.walkthrough: SANDER goes 'over' L (the last of quarrel) to make SLANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Britons live on islands, so a Brit is an inhabitant of the British Isles.

clue.text: Star exploding — somewhat taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback suggests the letters are read backwards
somewhat means only part of the word is used

explanation.surface: A star explodes and onlookers are rather startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes LODI from inside exploding; 'taken aback' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A star celebrity is someone adored by fans, an object of worship.

clue.text: King's picked up spoils

indicators.note: picked up means heard by the ear

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, used in the monarch's title; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A monarch gathers up the plunder of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' looks like a noun (loot) but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil something is to ruin or destroy it.

clue.text: State, traditionally powerful one, withdrawing quietly

indicators.note: withdrawing means taking out of the word

parts.note: Prussia was a historic military power in Germany
P is piano, the music notation for quiet

explanation.surface: A country that has long been a great power is quietly pulling back.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is a nation, and a state means a country with its own government.

clue.text: Quiet! Let one on board with keel close to waterline

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
to let is to allow
a draught is a piece on a draughts board, the British name for checkers

explanation.surface: Someone calls for silence and lets a passenger aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one on board' suggests a ship but means a piece in draughts (checkers).
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel's draught is how deep it sits; a shallow one barely dips below the surface.

clue.text: I don't like that Romeo — he's rude

parts.note: boo is a shout of disapproval
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone takes against a lover who has been impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: A boor is an ill-mannered, uncouth person, someone coarse in behaviour.

clue.text: Expecting medicine, sort of?

parts.note: expecting means pregnant, and the branch of medicine dealing with pregnancy and childbirth is the answer

explanation.surface: Someone hopes for a dose of some kind of remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' looks like waiting but means pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of medicine deals with pregnancy and childbirth, the care of women who are expecting.

clue.text: Barney and Betty getting wings clipped — very restricting

indicators.note: restricting means the letters for very close round the other piece

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: with its wings clipped a word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Barney and Betty, of the Flintstones, have their wings clipped and find it very restricting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting wings clipped' leaves ETT, which SO surrounds. A barney is British slang for a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A barney is a noisy quarrel, and a set-to is a brief fight or argument.

clue.text: Take care over truck being recorded

indicators.note: over means the word for take care covers the truck on both sides

parts.note: to mind is to take care, as in mind the step
a ute is a utility truck, the Australian pickup

explanation.surface: Drive carefully past the lorry being filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutes are the official notes of a meeting, so a minuted point has been written down.

clue.text: Poor bloke on the fiddle slightly twisted? Get away!

indicators.note: slightly twisted means two letters are turned round in place

parts.note: a scraper is a jokey name for a bad violinist

explanation.surface: A crooked chap who is fiddling the books is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' looks like cheating but means playing the violin. 'slightly twisted' swaps the R and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarper is British slang for running away, used here as a command to clear off.
